blocks.title: MIA — check bags & security
blocks.detail:
• Aer Lingus check-in, Terminal E
• Bags tag straight through to Paris — this is the only check-in of the outbound
• Three hours before departure is right for a holiday-week transatlantic

blocks.title: Early dinner at MIA
blocks.detail:
• Eat properly now — the on-board dinner service does not come round until about 9:00 PM
• Concourse E has a food court; sit-down options are slower and pricier
• Fill water bottles after security
blocks.notes: Airport food court for four, roughly $55–65.

blocks.title: Gate & boarding
blocks.detail:
• Toilets and pyjamas for the kids before boarding
• Anything they need overnight comes out of the bag now

blocks.title: Aer Lingus 140 · MIA → DUB (overnight)
blocks.detail:
• 8h15m, Airbus A330-300
• Dinner served about 2 hours in; light breakfast about an hour before landing
• Lands Dublin Terminal 2 at 8:20 AM
• Evening departure means the kids go down close to a normal bedtime
blocks.program: Aer Lingus award — currency to confirm
blocks.notes: 27,500 points + $29.10 per person. Four passengers = 110,000 points + $116.40. Fare class P, exactly 4 seats showing. Total elapsed MIA→CDG is 11h40m.
blocks.flag: Only 4 award seats — no margin. Confirm the points currency before assuming the balance covers it.

blocks.title: Dublin connection — 1h35m
blocks.detail:
• Both flights are Aer Lingus, both Terminal 2
• Follow 'Flight Connections' to passport control
• Bags move automatically on the single ticket; no second security screening
• Buy coffee and something for the kids here — nothing is available on arrival at CDG before immigration
blocks.flag: Under the 1h45m–2h Aer Lingus recommends for US arrivals continuing into Europe. A late EI140 threatens the Paris leg.

blocks.title: Aer Lingus 524 · DUB → CDG
blocks.detail:
• 1h50m, Airbus A320
• Arrives Paris Charles de Gaulle Terminal 1

blocks.title: CDG Terminal 1 — passport control & bags
blocks.detail:
• Ireland is outside Schengen, so this is a full external-border arrival
• EU Entry/Exit System: passport scan, photo and fingerprints for the adults
• Children under 12 are exempt from fingerprinting — photo and scan only
• Baggage claim is Level 5
• Keep snacks in hand luggage: the queue is where the kids will crack, not after
blocks.flag: T1 queues of 60–90 minutes have been reported at peak since EES rolled out, and 13:00–18:00 is a peak band. Budget up to 2 hours wheels-down to arrivals hall.

blocks.title: Lunch at CDG — McDonald's, public area
blocks.detail:
• Landside McDonald's, Terminal 1 public zone (CDGVAL level) — follow signs down from arrivals
• Open 06:00–22:00, 450 m², table service, ordering kiosks and a children's play area
• The only hot food at T1 with real seating and somewhere for the kids to burn off the flight
• Cheaper alternative if everyone is flagging: Marks & Spencer Food on the arrivals level (Level 5, 06:30–20:30) — sandwiches and fruit, grab-and-go, no detour
blocks.notes: About €40–45 for four. A Big Mac menu at CDG runs about €12.90 against €8.90 in town — airport markup is roughly 45%. M&S picnic instead would be about €30–35.

blocks.title: Back up to arrivals — taxi rank
blocks.detail:
• Official rank is Level 5 (arrivals), Exit 24, past the car-rental desks
• Use the marked rank only — ignore anyone offering a ride in the hall
• Uber/VTC pickup is a different place (Departures, Exit 16)

blocks.title: Taxi CDG → Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile
blocks.detail:
• Regulated flat rate: €56 Right Bank (Porte Maillot is the 17th)
• Covers up to 4 passengers, luggage included, no surcharges
• 30 km, 45–60 minutes
• Ask for a van (monospace) at the rank so all four fit in one car
blocks.notes: €56 flat rate. Beats RER B (€14/adult, €7/child = €42) once you add two changes and stairs with suitcases. Roissybus was permanently discontinued 28 Feb 2026.
blocks.flag: RER B is running reduced frequency through 2026 engineering works — another reason to take the taxi.

blocks.title: Check in — Hyatt Regency Paris Étoile, 4 nights, 2 rooms
blocks.detail:
• 3 Place du Général Kœnig, 75017 Paris
• Métro 1, RER C and RER E all run directly underneath
• Ask about Regency Club access for BOTH rooms — breakfast is the whole budget plan
• Request high floor, south-facing, connecting rooms
blocks.roomType: 2 rooms — high floor, Eiffel Tower view requested
blocks.notes: 15,000 points per room per night × 2 rooms × 4 nights = 120,000. Category 4: 12,000 off-peak / 15,000 standard / 18,000 peak.
blocks.flag: Confirm these dates don't price at Category 4 peak (18,000/night = 144,000 total), and that Regency Club breakfast covers the second room. Breakfast in the Mayo restaurant is €25 per person — €100 a morning if the lounge doesn't cover you.

blocks.title: Unpack & reset
blocks.detail:
• Everyone has been travelling about 22 hours
• Showers, unpack, no agenda
• Do not let the kids sleep now — push through to a normal bedtime

blocks.title: Short walk — Palais des Congrès & Christmas lights
blocks.detail:
• Straight out the hotel door, flat and lit
• Twenty minutes of fresh air is what resets a body clock
• Stop at the Monoprix or a bakery on the way back for tonight's supper

blocks.title: Supper in the room — picnic
blocks.detail:
• Baguette, ham, cheese, fruit, yoghurts, drinks from Monoprix or Franprix on avenue des Ternes
• Deliberate: nobody wants a restaurant on day one, and it costs a quarter of one
• Sit-down fallback next door is Le Congrès Maillot (80 av. de la Grande Armée, daily to midnight) — but it is a seafood brasserie and will run well over €100
blocks.notes: Supermarket picnic for four, roughly €25–30.

blocks.title: Early night
blocks.detail:
• Six hours ahead of Miami — the first night is the one that fixes the jet lag
• Lights out for the kids by 8:45

days.title: Tuileries Christmas market & the Champs-Élysées lights

blocks.title: Breakfast — Regency Club, 34th floor
blocks.detail:
• Included with the stay — this is the single biggest saving of the Paris leg
• Buffet breakfast with Eiffel Tower views
• Eat properly; lunch is not until about 12:45
blocks.notes: €0 if Regency Club access covers the family. The paid alternative is €25 per person in Mayo — €100 a morning.

blocks.title: Bois de Boulogne — morning walk
blocks.detail:
• Directly across from the hotel, no transport needed
• Flat paths, lakes, ducks; free
• Deliberately gentle — first full day after a transatlantic

blocks.title: Métro 1 · Porte Maillot → Concorde
blocks.detail:
• Line 1 from beneath the hotel, direction Château de Vincennes
• 6 stops, about 11 minutes, NO changes
• Line 1 is automated with platform screen doors — the easiest line in Paris with small children
• Buy Navigo Easy cards at the Porte Maillot window this morning (see the Ideas tab)
blocks.notes: Day's fares: 2 adults €2.55 each + 2 children (4–9) €1.30 each = €7.70 each way, €15.40 return. Cards €2 each, bought once.

blocks.title: Tuileries Christmas Market — La Magie de Noël
blocks.detail:
• Jardin des Tuileries, north side, 1st arr. — exit Concorde and it is right there
• FREE entry. About 100 chalets, carousel, toddler train, bumper cars, fun houses
• Open from 11:00
• Getting back: Métro 1 from Concorde or Tuileries, direct to Porte Maillot
blocks.flag: 2026–27 dates are not yet published. The 2025–26 edition ran 15 Nov – 4 Jan, so your dates almost certainly fall inside — re-check in November. Guaranteed fallback: La Défense market, confirmed 12 Nov – 31 Dec 2026, four stops on Métro 1.

blocks.title: Lunch — market chalets, Tuileries
blocks.detail:
• Eat at the market: crêpes, hot dogs, tartiflette, churros, hot chocolate
• Warm, quick, no reservation, and the kids choose their own
• Cheaper still: buy baguette sandwiches at a bakery near the hotel before leaving and eat them in the gardens
blocks.notes: Market food for four, roughly €30–38. Crêpe €5–7, vin chaud €5–6, hot dog €7–9, churros €5 — estimates, no market publishes a tariff.

blocks.title: Tuileries rides & carousel
blocks.detail:
• Pick TWO things, not all of them — the rides add up fast
• Carousel and small rides about €3–5 per child per go
• Ice rink is €10 adult / €6 child = €32 for four if you want a bigger one
• Skip the Ferris wheel — €15 a head with no child rate
blocks.notes: Budget €20 for a few goes on the carousel and rides. Ride prices are estimates — nothing is published.

blocks.title: Walk — Tuileries → Concorde → Champs-Élysées
blocks.detail:
• Out the west end of the gardens, across Place de la Concorde
• Then up the Champs-Élysées as far as the kids want — it is 1.9 km end to end, you do not need to walk it all
• Dark by about 5:00 PM

blocks.title: Champs-Élysées Christmas illuminations
blocks.detail:
• Lights switch on at 17:00 and run to midnight (1:00 AM Fri and Sat)
• Free. The trees down both sides of the avenue are the whole point
• Then walk to Franklin D. Roosevelt métro for dinner

blocks.title: Métro to dinner
blocks.detail:
• Métro 1 from Franklin D. Roosevelt → 1 stop to Franklin D. Roosevelt interchange, then Métro 9 direction Mairie de Montreuil → Grands Boulevards
• About 15 minutes total

blocks.title: Dinner — Bouillon Chartier, Grands Boulevards
blocks.detail:
• 7 rue du Faubourg Montmartre, 75009 · Métro Grands Boulevards
• Historic 1896 dining hall, open daily 11:30–00:00, NO reservations — go early to beat the queue
• Mains from €7: roast chicken €10.50, confit de canard €12.50, steak with pepper sauce €13.20
• Starters from €1, desserts from €2, green beans €2.60
• No formal children's menu, but roast chicken and plain sides work perfectly
• This is the cheapest genuinely memorable meal in Paris
blocks.notes: About €70–80 for four including drinks. A comparable meal in a Rue Cler bistro would be €130–140.

blocks.title: Métro back to the hotel
blocks.detail:
• Métro 9 → Franklin D. Roosevelt, change to Métro 1 → Porte Maillot
• About 25 minutes

days.title: Eiffel Tower, Trocadéro & a Seine cruise

blocks.title: Breakfast — Regency Club
blocks.detail:
• Included
• Today is the biggest walking day — eat well
• Grab fruit for pockets on the way out

blocks.title: RER C · Neuilly–Porte Maillot → Champ de Mars–Tour Eiffel
blocks.detail:
• RER C runs directly beneath the hotel — this is the hidden advantage of Porte Maillot
• DIRECT, 4 stops, 11–12 minutes, no changes and no stair interchange
• Trains about every 15 minutes
• Same €2.55 / €1.30 fare as one métro stop

blocks.title: Champ de Mars & the Eiffel Tower from below
blocks.detail:
• The tower straight up from the lawns — free, and the view children actually remember
• Carousel at the base
• NOT going up: €59 for four to the 2nd floor, cold, queued, and dark by 16:00. Trocadéro next is the better picture and costs nothing

blocks.title: Pont d'Iéna → Trocadéro
blocks.detail:
• Cross the bridge and climb to Place du Trocadéro — the classic Eiffel photograph
• Quai Branly Christmas market sits along the river on the way
• Flat, about 15 minutes at child pace

blocks.title: Lunch — Quai Branly Christmas market
blocks.detail:
• Market chalets along the river: crêpes, sausages, tartiflette, hot chocolate
• Warm and quick, and it avoids the 7th arrondissement restaurant trap
• DO NOT eat sit-down near the tower: the cheapest Rue Cler plat du jour is €16–17 a head, so €65+ before drinks
blocks.notes: Roughly €35–42 for four. Market dates for 2026 unconfirmed — if it is not running, the bakery-picnic fallback is to buy near the hotel before boarding the RER.
blocks.flag: Quai Branly market 2026 dates unpublished. Carry a bakery lunch as backup.

blocks.title: Walk Trocadéro → Pont de l'Alma
blocks.detail:
• Down the hill along avenue du Président Wilson, about 15 minutes
• Time in hand before the boat — there is a warm café at the embarkation point

blocks.title: Seine cruise — Bateaux Mouches
blocks.detail:
• Departs Port de la Conférence, Pont de l'Alma, 8th arr.
• 1 hour, heated glass-roofed boat, seated — the warmest hour of the day
• BOOK ONLINE: €17 adult / €8 child (under 13) = €50 for four. At the pier it is €20/€10 = €60
• Under 4 free
• Timed so you leave in daylight and come back as the lights come on
blocks.notes: €50 booked online. Vedettes du Pont Neuf is €44 but departs from Île de la Cité, which does not fit this day.

blocks.title: Warm up — hot chocolate
blocks.detail:
• Café near the quay before the métro
• Everyone will be cold off the water

blocks.title: Métro back to the hotel
blocks.detail:
• Métro 9 from Alma–Marceau → Franklin D. Roosevelt
• Change to Métro 1 → Porte Maillot
• About 20 minutes, one change

blocks.title: Supper in the room — picnic
blocks.detail:
• Monoprix or Franprix on avenue des Ternes: rotisserie chicken, baguette, salad, cheese, fruit, yoghurts
• Second picnic night of the trip, and deliberate — today was a long cold day and tomorrow is another full one
• Costs about a third of a restaurant
blocks.notes: Roughly €25–30 for four.

blocks.title: Breakfast — Regency Club
blocks.detail:
• Included
• Last Paris breakfast before the train day

blocks.title: Métro · Porte Maillot → Anvers
blocks.detail:
• Métro 1 → Charles de Gaulle–Étoile (1 stop, 2 min)
• Change to Métro 2, direction Nation → Anvers (8 stops, ~14 min)
• About 22 minutes total, one change
• Exit Anvers and walk up rue de Steinkerque towards the basilica

blocks.title: Montmartre funicular
blocks.detail:
• Saves about 200 steps with a 5-year-old — worth every cent
• Takes a standard Métro ticket: €2.55 adult, €1.30 child = €7.70 for four, one way
• Note: the ticket does NOT let you transfer to another mode afterwards

blocks.title: Sacré-Cœur & the terrace
blocks.detail:
• Entry to the basilica is completely FREE, open 06:30–22:30 daily
• The terrace in front is one of the great free views in Paris — the whole city laid out
• Carousel at the foot of the hill
• Skipping the dome climb: €26 for four and 280 steps with no lift, not realistic with a 5-year-old

blocks.title: Lunch — Bouillon Pigalle
blocks.detail:
• 22 boulevard de Clichy, 75018 · about 10 minutes downhill from Sacré-Cœur
• Open 7 days, 12:00–00:00 — one of the few reliable Sunday options
• Œuf mayonnaise €2.50, onion soup €3.90, sausage & mash €9.60, bœuf bourguignon €12.20, steak-frites €12.60, duck confit €12.80
• Fries €3.00, rice pudding €2.80, crème brûlée €3.80, soft drinks €1.10–2.60
• No kids' menu, but sausage-and-mash at €9.60 is the children's dish
• No reservations — arrive at 12:00 to avoid the queue
blocks.notes: About €60–68 for four. Menu prices from the official card; a 2026 guide confirms mains still €9.80–12.20, so add ~10% margin.

blocks.title: Place du Tertre & the Montmartre back streets
blocks.detail:
• Street artists on the square, then the quieter lanes behind — rue de l'Abreuvoir, the vineyard, the Wall of Love
• Abbesses Christmas market at Place des Abbesses if running
• All free; this is a wander, not a schedule

blocks.title: Crêpe stop
blocks.detail:
• Street crêpe stands all over Montmartre — €4–6 each
• Bridges the gap to a light supper

blocks.title: Métro back to the hotel
blocks.detail:
• Walk down to Anvers or Pigalle
• Métro 2 → Charles de Gaulle–Étoile, change to Métro 1 → Porte Maillot
• About 25 minutes

blocks.title: Light supper in the room & pack
blocks.detail:
• Picnic from the Monoprix — nothing heavy, tomorrow starts early
• Repack tonight: winter gear and snow clothes go to the top of the bags for Chamonix
• Passports out and accessible — tomorrow crosses into Switzerland

blocks.title: Lights out
blocks.detail:
• Tomorrow is a 5h30 travel day with a 8:45 AM hotel departure
• Working back from a 7:15 breakfast: bedtime now

blocks.title: Breakfast — Regency Club
blocks.detail:
• Included. Eat a real breakfast — the next proper meal is a picnic on the train around noon
• Fill water bottles
• Take a couple of pastries for the taxi

blocks.title: Checkout
blocks.detail:
• Bags down, checkout, hold nothing back
• Confirm the taxi at the door

blocks.title: Taxi · hotel → Gare de Lyon
blocks.detail:
• Métro 1 goes there direct in ~25 minutes, but with four people and winter luggage in Monday rush hour the taxi is the right call
• About €25–30
• Missing this train breaks the whole day — do not economise here

blocks.title: Gare de Lyon — buy the train picnic
blocks.detail:
• TGV Lyria departs EXCLUSIVELY from Hall 2 — buy in Hall 2 and stay there
• Monop'Daily, Hall 2 Level 0, open 06:00–22:00: sandwiches, fruit, yoghurts, crisps, drinks in one transaction
• Paul and Maison Pradier alongside for fresh baguettes
• Cheaper: the Monoprix across rue de Lyon, or Franprix in the Galerie Diderot (level −1) — but both are a walk with bags
• Platform posts about 20 minutes before departure, so around 09:58
blocks.notes: Family picnic about €40–50 at Monop'Daily, or €25–35 at the Monoprix opposite the station. For comparison, four Menu Sandwich combos in the train bar car cost €54.

blocks.title: TGV Lyria 9765 · Paris Gare de Lyon → Genève Cornavin
blocks.detail:
• 3h18, calling Bourg-en-Bresse 12:12 and Bellegarde 12:59
• Passports out — this crosses into Switzerland
• Eat the picnic about 12:00
• Bar car 'Le Bistrot' is on the UPPER deck, 2nd class: no at-seat service, you go to it. Hot chocolate €4.50, croissant €2.70, club sandwich €7.50, Menu Sandwich (sandwich + dessert + drink) €13.50
• Good move: at about 11:15, before the lunch rush, one adult takes one child up for hot chocolates — it breaks the journey and costs under €15
• Bringing your own food is fine. Swiss customs explicitly allow ready-to-eat food for the day of travel
blocks.notes: Family estimate with one Carte Avantage Adulte (€49): about €174 for four at a €79 base fare, against €316 without the card. Lyria Standard fares open around €49 and climb like an airfare.
blocks.flag: Times are the current-season pattern. The 13 December 2026 timetable recast has not published and sales open 30 September 2026. Re-verify then.

blocks.title: Bar-car snack & Cornavin arrival
blocks.detail:
• Lyria arrives on platforms 7 or 8 at Genève Cornavin
• If anyone is still hungry: Migros inside the station (East Wing, 06:00–22:00 daily) is the cheap option
• Switzerland is expensive — a cheap restaurant meal is about CHF 25 (€26) a head. Do not eat a sit-down lunch here

blocks.title: Walk Cornavin → Gare Routière, Place Dorcière
blocks.detail:
• About 350 m via rue du Mont-Blanc or rue des Alpes
• Ten minutes for an adult — budget twenty with two children and bags
• City bus 9 or 25 covers it in two stops in bad weather
• You never go near the airport: both FlixBus and Swiss Tours use the city-centre coach station

blocks.title: Bus Geneva → Chamonix
blocks.detail:
• 1h10–1h25 up the valley
• FlixBus runs nine city-centre departures daily 04:35–22:35; Swiss Tours eleven, 08:00–20:30, usually €11–17 per person
• Book FlixBus for free cancellation — a late TGV otherwise forfeits the fare
• Get off at Chamonix Centre (414 Allée Recteur Payot), NOT Chamonix Sud
blocks.flag: No through-ticketing between the train and the bus. Do not book a bus leaving before about 14:30 — you want an hour of buffer on the Lyria arrival.

blocks.title: Walk to the hotel
blocks.detail:
• Chamonix Centre stop is next to the SNCF station, about four minutes from the hotel
• Dark by about 4:50 PM and likely icy — boots with grip, not travel shoes

blocks.title: Check in — Pointe Isabelle, 6 nights
blocks.detail:
• 165 Avenue Michel Croz — 3 minutes to the SNCF and Montenvers stations, 4 to the centre
• ASK FOR THE CARTE D'HÔTE at the desk: free, and it gives unlimited free travel on the Mont-Blanc Express between Servoz and Vallorcine for the whole stay
• Request a rear or courtyard-facing room — the street side is loud from the bars
• Top-floor sauna, gym, bar-bistro downstairs
blocks.notes: €1,668 for six nights including taxes — about €278 a night — fully refundable at time of research. 9.0/10 across 520 reviews. Breakfast is NOT included and is not the plan: see the supermarket shop below.
blocks.flag: See the Ideas tab for cheaper and better-equipped alternatives, including Hôtel l'Oustalet (heated outdoor pool, ~€1,715) and self-catering options.

blocks.title: Super U shop — the week's breakfasts and picnics
blocks.detail:
• Super U, 117 rue Joseph Vallot — 6–8 minutes' walk, open Mon–Sat 08:15–19:30
• This one shop is what keeps the Chamonix food budget under control
• Buy: bread, croissants, butter, jam, cereal, milk, coffee, juice, fruit, yoghurts, ham, cheese, crisps, chocolate, water bottles
• Six days of in-room breakfasts and packed lunches costs about €140–220 here, against €400–700 buying those meals out
blocks.notes: Big arrival shop about €70–110. Top up midweek as needed.

blocks.title: Dinner — Elevation 1904
blocks.detail:
• Directly opposite the main train station, about 3 minutes from the hotel
• Open 07:30–01:30 daily, year-round
• Burgers, sandwiches, comfort food; reasonably priced and used to families
• Shortest possible walk on a night when everyone has been travelling since 7:00 AM
blocks.notes: About €55–65 for four. Prices not published — this is an estimate.

blocks.title: Breakfast in the room
blocks.detail:
• From yesterday's Super U shop: bread, croissants, cereal, fruit, juice, coffee
• Adults: coffee is enough if you prefer
• About €10–12 for the four of you, against €58 in a hotel dining room

blocks.title: Chamonix town on foot
blocks.detail:
• Deliberate recovery day — nothing today needs a bus
• Pedestrian centre, Maison de la Montagne, the bridges over the Arve with the Aiguilles above
• Christmas lights and shop windows
• All free, all within ten minutes of the hotel

blocks.title: Back to the hotel — into snow gear
blocks.detail:
• Deliberate changeover block
• Sledging means snow down collars and wet gloves — change properly now, not at the park
• Spare gloves and socks in a bag

blocks.title: Lunch — Poco Loco
blocks.detail:
• 47 rue du Docteur Paccard, open daily 10:00–22:00 (Tue from 10:30)
• A Chamonix institution since 1996: burgers, fries, hot sandwiches, crêpes
• Takeaway counter, no bookings, fast — exactly right before an afternoon outdoors
• Burgers roughly €9–14
blocks.notes: About €45–55 for four. Menu prices not published — estimate.

blocks.title: Les Planards — Alpine Coaster & sledging
blocks.detail:
• 351 chemin du Pied du Grépon — 9 minutes on foot behind the Montenvers station, no transport needed
• Coaster: 1.3 km of banked rail, 540° spirals, rider-controlled brake so you set the speed
• Runs 11:00–17:30 daily in winter, lit in the evening over Christmas
• Dedicated toboggan slopes at the base — this is the sledging day of the trip
• BOTH children must ride with an adult: minimum height to ride alone is 1.35 m
• 6-ride pack €47.50 (5+1 free) = three family descents
blocks.flag: Sledging-area hours, access price and whether sledges are hired or sold could not be confirmed — the Planards site was down throughout research. Phone before you go.

blocks.title: Hot chocolate at the base café
blocks.detail:
• Halfway through the afternoon, before anyone gets cold and miserable
• Café on site at Les Planards

blocks.title: Back to the hotel — dry off, sauna
blocks.detail:
• Wet gear out to dry properly — it has to last five more days
• Top-floor sauna with rooftop views, exactly right after three hours outdoors

blocks.title: Dinner — Pointe Isabelle bar & bistro
blocks.detail:
• Downstairs in your own hotel — no walk in the cold at either end
• Mixed menu: meat, fish, vegetarian and Savoyard, open daily
• Worth doing on the first full day; you will want the short walk
blocks.notes: About €60–68 for four. Prices not published — estimate.

blocks.title: Breakfast in the room
blocks.detail:
• The one early start of the stay, and it buys a full day out of the valley
• Make up packed snacks for the bus while you are at it

blocks.title: Walk to the bus stop
blocks.detail:
• Chamonix Sud, 234 Avenue de Courmayeur — twelve minutes from the hotel
• Some services also call at Chamonix Centre (Allée Recteur Payot), four minutes away — check which your ticket uses

blocks.title: Bus Chamonix → Annecy
blocks.detail:
• 1h10 direct, down the valley and out of the mountains
• Arrives at the bus station, 3 Place de la Gare, beside the SNCF station
• BlaBlaCar Bus from €7.99, about ten connections a day, free exchange/refund up to 30 days out
• Some services stop at Bonlieu — two minutes from the Pont des Amours. Take that one if offered
blocks.notes: Roughly €64–74 return for the family. FlixBus runs three a day from about €11.63.
blocks.flag: December departure times are not published yet. The window runs 06:00–17:00 outbound and to 22:05 returning, so the day works — book exact times as soon as they load.

blocks.title: Pont des Amours, Le Pâquier & the lakefront
blocks.detail:
• Coldest part of the day, so keep moving
• Pont des Amours crosses the Canal du Vassé — the postcard view
• Le Pâquier is the big lakeside meadow with swans and ducks year-round; bring seed, not bread
• Flat, pushchair-friendly, mountains across the water. All free

blocks.title: The old town & the canals
blocks.detail:
• Canal du Thiou, Quai de l'Île, rue Sainte-Claire, rue Perrière
• Arcaded, pedestrian, lit and strung with Christmas lights
• This is what Annecy is famous for; about an hour with children and stops

blocks.title: Lunch — Chez Mamie Lise
blocks.detail:
• 11 rue Grenette, in the old town on the square with Santa's meet-and-greet
• Open daily 11:45–14:00
• ORDER THE PLAT DU JOUR at €19 — the à la carte mains are €25–40 and will double the bill
• Children's menu €18: steak, chicken nuggets or ham with a side and dessert
• Reserve on +33 4 50 45 41 18
blocks.notes: Two plats du jour at €19 plus two children's menus at €18 = €74 before drinks. Ordering à la carte instead pushes this past €130.

blocks.title: Jardins de l'Europe & the ice rink
blocks.detail:
• Lakeside park at the mouth of the Thiou, and the main Christmas market site in December
• 460 m² natural ice rink with skate hire on site, and in prior years a slower zone for young children
• Getting back later: the bus station is a 10-minute walk from here
blocks.flag: 2026 rink prices are not published. Expect roughly €6–8 per person including skates — an estimate.

blocks.title: Snack — crêpes and vin chaud
blocks.detail:
• Market chalets as the light goes
• Bridges the gap to a late supper back in Chamonix

blocks.title: Noël des Alpes Christmas market
blocks.detail:
• Dusk falls about 16:50 — that is when the market is at its best
• 135 artisan chalets across the town centre and the Jardins de l'Europe
• Illuminations on the historic buildings, Santa Claus meet-and-greet, Savoyard food, vin chaud
• FREE entry. Confirmed dates: 26 Nov 2026 – 3 Jan 2027, 11:00–21:00

blocks.title: Bus back to Chamonix
blocks.detail:
• Ten-minute walk from the market to the bus station
• Back in Chamonix around 20:00

blocks.title: Late supper in the room
blocks.detail:
• Nothing cooked — bread, cheese, ham, fruit from the Super U shop
• No walk, no booking, straight to bed after a long day
• Tomorrow crosses into Italy: passports out tonight

days.title: Courmayeur, Italy — tubing, then Christmas Eve

blocks.title: Breakfast in the room
blocks.detail:
• PASSPORTS for all four today — France and Italy are both Schengen, but the bus operators require ID
• Pack snacks: the Courmayeur supermarket shuts 13:00–15:30

blocks.title: Walk to Chamonix Sud
blocks.detail:
• 234 Avenue de Courmayeur, twelve minutes from the hotel
• The SAT Mont Blanc coach leaves from here

blocks.title: SAT bus · Chamonix → Courmayeur
blocks.detail:
• About 45 minutes through the 11.6 km Mont Blanc tunnel to Piazzale Monte Bianco
• You come out in Italy — different language, different food, same mountain from the other side
• €30 adult / €15 child 0–12 same-day return = €90 for the family
blocks.flag: BOOKING IS MANDATORY by 17:00 the previous day via savda.it or estore.arriva.it — book it on the 22nd, not the 23rd when you are in Annecy. Winter 2026/27 timetable unpublished: phone +33 4 50 78 05 33 or +39 0165 367039 for actual times.

blocks.title: Fun Park Dolonne — tubing & bobsled track
blocks.detail:
• Strada Chécrouit 9, a short walk or free shuttle from Piazzale Monte Bianco
• The reason to come: a proper TUBING run and a bobsled/sledge track
• Plus soft inflatables, trampolines, carousels and slides for when the 5-year-old has had enough of the cold
• Beginner slope with three magic-carpet lifts if anyone wants a first go on skis
• Café on site
• Neither Chamonix nor the French side of the valley has a tubing run — this is the only one within reach
blocks.notes: Prices unpublished; reportedly you can pay per activity rather than buying a day pass, which suits a half-day.
blocks.flag: Prices, hours, minimum ages AND 24 December opening are all unverified. Phone +39 366 268 6776 or email funpark.dolonne@gmail.com before travelling — Christmas Eve hours may be short.

blocks.title: Lunch — Via Roma, Courmayeur
blocks.detail:
• La Padella, Vicolo Dolonne 7 (+39 0165 841877) — fixed-price menus described as abundant and economical. Best value in town
• Or La Terrazza, Via Circonvallazione 73 (+39 0165 843330) — pizza and traditional fare
• Cheapest: prepared food from Pastificio Gabriella, Via Roma 102, or the Carrefour Express deli counter
• Italy runs roughly 20–30% below French alpine prices — pizzas €8–13 against €12–17 in Chamonix
blocks.notes: Sit-down pizza lunch for four about €45–65; deli/takeaway about €25–40. Courmayeur menu prices could not be verified.
blocks.flag: Carrefour Express closes 13:00–15:30 — buy before 13:00 if you want the supermarket option.

blocks.title: Via Roma & the village
blocks.detail:
• Courmayeur's pedestrian main street — genuinely Italian, not French-alpine
• Shops, the church square, Mont Blanc from the Italian side, gelato even in December
• Deliberately no second ticketed activity — the morning was the event

blocks.title: SAT bus back to Chamonix
blocks.detail:
• Return leg of the same booking
• Back at Chamonix Sud around 16:30, twelve minutes' walk from the hotel

blocks.title: Back at the hotel — warm up and change
blocks.detail:
• Unstructured, then into something decent for Christmas Eve
• Presents organised for the morning

blocks.title: Christmas Eve dinner
blocks.detail:
• One of the two proper meals of the trip — worth the money
• Chamonix restaurants run FIXED festive menus on the 24th and they sell out. Book in November
• Pointe Isabelle restaurant (165 Av. Michel Croz, +33 4 50 53 12 87) publishes separate 24 and 25 December menus
• Le Cap Horn (74 rue des Moulins, +33 4 50 21 80 80) runs a festive service every season
• Expect €70–120 per adult with à la carte withdrawn; several venues offer no child price at all
blocks.notes: Budgeted at about €150 for four. This and Christmas dinner are the two splurges — every other meal is held down to compensate.
blocks.flag: No Chamonix venue has published 2026 festive menus; they appear early-to-mid November. Call the week they open — these sell out.

blocks.title: Breakfast & presents in the room
blocks.detail:
• No fixed start today
• Everything today is built around things that CANNOT close: lifts, snow and the valley train
• Assume no shop is open — you shopped on the 23rd for this

blocks.title: Walk to the Planpraz gondola
blocks.detail:
• Brévent–Planpraz base is on the north edge of the centre, about ten minutes from the hotel
• Walkable, no bus needed — which matters on a day when buses thin out

blocks.title: Gondola to Planpraz, 2,000 m
blocks.detail:
• A sun-facing shelf directly opposite Mont Blanc — the classic postcard angle
• Lifts DO run on Christmas Day; it is their peak revenue week
• Pedestrian return: family pass €77.60, or adult €25.00 and child 5–14 €18.00 separately. Under 5 free
• Skip the top section to Brévent (2,525 m) — colder, windier, a further €66 for four
blocks.flag: Fares shown are the summer 2026 sheet; the winter grid publishes around November.

blocks.title: Snow play at Planpraz
blocks.detail:
• Deep snow, wide open ground, a big sunny terrace, the valley floor a thousand metres below
• Snowmen, snowball fights, room to run
• Being straight: Planpraz is a ski-area mid-station, NOT a snow park. There is no toboggan run here — do not promise the kids sledging. Tuesday at Les Planards was the sledging

blocks.title: Lunch — packed, at La Bergerie de Planpraz
blocks.detail:
• Carry sandwiches and snacks up from the Super U shop
• Buy hot drinks and maybe one hot dish at La Bergerie, the mountain restaurant at the top station, so you have somewhere warm to sit
• A full mountain-restaurant lunch on Christmas Day would be €110–130 for four; this way it is about €35
blocks.flag: Confirm La Bergerie is open on 25 December — mountain restaurants usually are during the holiday week, but it is not verified.

blocks.title: Gondola down
blocks.detail: • Last descent is 17:00, so there is no pressure

blocks.title: Mont-Blanc Express to Argentière — free
blocks.detail:
• The Carte d'Hôte makes the valley train FREE between Servoz and Vallorcine — no tickets, turn up and go
• Argentière is fifteen minutes up the line at 1,250 m: smaller, quieter, deeper snow, easy to walk around
• Come back whenever everyone has had enough — trains run about hourly
• Costs nothing, which on Christmas Day when everything is shut is exactly what you want

blocks.title: Hot chocolate in Argentière
blocks.detail: • Before the train back down

blocks.title: Back at the hotel — warm up and change
blocks.detail: • Quiet end to the afternoon before dinner

blocks.title: Christmas dinner
blocks.detail:
• The second of the two proper meals — book it in November alongside Christmas Eve
• FAR fewer places open on the 25th than the 24th, and those that do run one fixed menu at a set price
• Pointe Isabelle restaurant publishes a separate 25 December menu: +33 4 50 53 12 87
• Fallback if nothing can be booked: your own hotel bistro, or a traiteur meal collected on Christmas morning
blocks.notes: Budgeted at about €130 for four.
blocks.flag: Christmas Day is the hardest booking of the trip. Reports conflict on how much of Chamonix opens — assume little, and reserve weeks ahead.

days.title: Mer de Glace, ice cave & skating

blocks.title: Breakfast in the room
blocks.detail:
• Last full day, and deliberately the easiest: everything today is within a fifteen-minute walk
• No bus, no border, nothing that can strand you the day before a travel day

blocks.title: Walk to the Montenvers station
blocks.detail:
• Four minutes — the cogwheel station is immediately beside the SNCF station, right by the hotel
• Buy at the ticket office, where the family pass and the under-5 exemption get applied

blocks.title: Montenvers Railway — the red train
blocks.detail:
• Twenty minutes of cogwheel railway through snow-covered pine to 1,913 m, opening onto the Mer de Glace
• First train of the day — worth it for the light and the empty platforms
• Voyage Mer de Glace family pass €148.30 covers train, gondola, ice cave and museums for all four
• Buying separately would be €183.80, so the family pass saves about €35
• Under 5 free with proof of age at the office
blocks.flag: Winter 2026/27 fares are not published — these are prior-season figures. Expect 3–5% higher.

blocks.title: Gondola down & the Grotte de Glace
blocks.detail:
• Gondola from 1,913 m down to 1,760 m, then a staircase to the cave carved fresh into the glacier each autumn
• About 170 steps down and the same back up — roughly a ten-storey climb on open metal treads that can ice up
• Hold hands. Expect to carry the 5-year-old part of the way back
• No pushchairs and no lift alternative
blocks.flag: The ice cave opens only days before you arrive — indicated from 13 December, but in 2025/26 it slipped to the 20th. Re-verify in late November. The train and the glacier viewpoint stand on their own if it has not opened.

blocks.title: Train back down
blocks.detail: • Twenty minutes. Last ascent 16:00, last descent 16:30 — no pressure this early

blocks.title: Lunch — Aux Petits Gourmands
blocks.detail:
• 168 rue du Docteur Paccard, about nine minutes on foot
• Pâtisserie and tea salon with real savoury options — quiches, sandwiches, salads — so it works as lunch, not just a sugar stop
• Open every day 07:30–19:30
• Cheaper alternative two minutes away: La Panière bakery, 31 Place de l'Église, opens 06:00 — filled baguettes about €5–7
blocks.notes: About €40–48 for four. Bakery alternative would be €22–30.

blocks.title: Back to the hotel — thick socks for the rink
blocks.detail: • Changeover block. Snow gear off and drying, normal clothes and proper socks on

blocks.title: Ice skating — Patinoire Richard Bozon
blocks.detail:
• 214 avenue de la Plage — about fifteen minutes on foot, or one stop on the bus to Médiathèque
• Olympic-size indoor rink, 60 m × 30 m. Public session 14:00–18:00 daily through the holidays
• Entry €6.80 adult, €5.00 child, UNDER 6 FREE — so the 5-year-old is free and the 7-year-old pays €5
• Skate hire €4.50 each. About €36.60 for four
• Carte d'Hôte gets a reduced rate — take it
blocks.flag: Whether this rink has penguin-style support frames could not be confirmed — they are documented at the Les Houches rink, not this one. Phone +33 4 50 53 12 36.

blocks.title: Back at the hotel — pack
blocks.detail:
• Pack tonight, properly. Tomorrow is bus-then-train with a tight walk in Geneva
• Wet gear into plastic bags
• Buy tomorrow's breakfast and travel snacks now — Super U closes 19:30 and Sunday it is mornings only

blocks.title: Dinner — Bighorn Bistro & Bakery
blocks.detail:
• 77 place Edmond Desailloud, Chamonix Sud
• Family-run American bistro that bakes its own bread: Bighorn burger €20, Peruvian chicken burger €20, Savoyard mac & cheese €15, bowls €18
• Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options
• Open Saturday from 16:00 — it closes Monday and Tuesday, so tonight is one of the nights it works
• Reserve on +33 7 89 07 79 62
blocks.notes: About €65–70 for four. A kids' menu exists but the price is not published.

blocks.title: Breakfast in the room
blocks.detail:
• Use up whatever is left from the Super U shop
• Next proper meal is about 13:30 at Geneva — that is the plan, not an accident

blocks.title: Finish packing
blocks.detail:
• Passports out and accessible — today crosses into Switzerland
• Checkout is 11:00; the bus is not until midday, so there is slack

blocks.title: Checkout — and buy the bus ticket ONLINE
blocks.detail:
• CRITICAL: Chamonix Sud bus station is unstaffed on Sundays with no ticket machines
• Buy the Geneva ticket online before you leave the hotel
• Hand the Carte d'Hôte back
blocks.flag: There is nobody at the station on a Sunday. Do not plan to buy on the day.

blocks.title: Buy the travelling lunch — La Panière
blocks.detail:
• 31 Place de l'Église (or 118 rue Whymper), opens 06:00
• Filled baguettes, quiches, pastries, drinks — about €5–7 a sandwich
• Buy it HERE, not in Geneva: Switzerland is about 25% more expensive and a cheap Geneva restaurant meal is CHF 25 (€26) a head
• You will eat this at Cornavin around 13:30
blocks.notes: About €28–32 for four, against roughly €105 for the same meal sat down in Geneva.

blocks.title: Walk to Chamonix Sud
blocks.detail:
• Twelve minutes with luggage
• Taxi fallback +33 4 50 53 13 94 if the weather has turned

blocks.title: Bus Chamonix → Genève, Place Dorcière
blocks.detail:
• 1h20 back down the valley
• Allow a generous buffer — the Chamonix–Geneva road on a changeover Sunday in ski season can add thirty minutes or more

blocks.title: Walk Place Dorcière → Genève Cornavin
blocks.detail:
• 350 m, fifteen to twenty minutes with children and luggage
• Lyria advises extra time boarding at Geneva because of border formalities — documents out

blocks.title: Lunch at Cornavin
blocks.detail:
• Eat the baguettes you bought in Chamonix — seating in the station concourse
• If you need to top up: Migros in the East Wing, open 06:00–22:00 EVERY day including Sunday, which is unusual in Switzerland
• Coop to go in the West Wing, 05:30–23:00
• Lyria departs from platforms 7 or 8

blocks.title: TGV Lyria 9774 · Genève → Paris Gare de Lyon
blocks.detail:
• 3h15, calling Bellegarde 15:02, arriving Gare de Lyon 17:42
• Bar car 'Le Bistrot' upper deck for a mid-journey snack around 16:30 — hot chocolate €4.50, cookie €4.00, croissant €2.70
• Long gap to dinner, so plan that snack rather than arriving starving
blocks.notes: Same Carte Avantage discounts as the outbound — roughly €174 for four.
blocks.flag: Sunday loses three of the eight Geneva–Paris departures: no 06:28, 10:27 or 12:27, leaving a six-hour hole between 08:21 and 14:27. The 14:27 is the only civilised option — book it the moment sales open on 30 September. Fallback is the 16:23, arriving 19:42.

blocks.title: Bar-car snack
blocks.detail:
• One adult and one child go up — it breaks the journey
• Keeps everyone going until dinner at about 19:45

blocks.title: Gare de Lyon — bags to the taxi rank
blocks.detail: • Straight out to the rank on the boulevard Diderot side

blocks.title: Taxi Gare de Lyon → Hyatt House CDG
blocks.detail:
• Roughly 35 km north-east, 45–60 minutes on a Sunday evening
• The CDG flat rate does NOT apply in this direction to a hotel outside the airport perimeter — expect a metered €70–90
• RER D then RER B is the cheap alternative at about an hour, but with four people, luggage and a long day behind you, take the taxi
blocks.flag: Metered, not flat-rate — Sunday evening traffic varies. Ask the hotel whether its airport shuttle can pick up, which would make this free.

blocks.title: Check in — Hyatt House Paris Charles de Gaulle
blocks.detail:
• Kitchenette-equipped suites, free airport shuttle, about fifteen minutes from the terminals
• CONFIRM the first shuttle departure tonight — you need to be at CDG by about 06:40
• Ask whether breakfast service starts early enough for a 06:15 departure; if not, buy something tonight
blocks.notes: 15,000 points for the night as given.
blocks.flag: Confirm whether 15,000 covers one room or two. The Paris stay uses two rooms; if this night needs two as well, it is 30,000.

blocks.title: Dinner at the hotel
blocks.detail:
• No excursion tonight. Bags repacked, boarding passes out, early night
• Buy tomorrow's early breakfast now if the shuttle beats the breakfast service

blocks.title: Wake & quick breakfast
blocks.detail:
• Whatever you bought last night, eaten in the room — the hotel breakfast service may not have started
• A proper breakfast is served on board about an hour after take-off

blocks.title: Shuttle to CDG Terminal 2E
blocks.detail:
• Free hotel shuttle, about fifteen minutes
• Confirm the first run at check-in the night before — if it starts later than 06:15, book a taxi instead
blocks.flag: Verify the shuttle's first departure. An airport shuttle that starts at 07:00 does not work for a 9:10 flight.

blocks.title: CDG — check in, security, passport control
blocks.detail:
• Delta departs Terminal 2E
• Schengen EXIT control plus US-bound security screening — allow the full window
• Two and a half hours is right for a transatlantic with four people and checked bags

blocks.title: Delta 83 · CDG → Atlanta
blocks.detail:
• Transatlantic leg, arriving Atlanta early afternoon local time
• Breakfast served shortly after take-off, second service before landing
blocks.notes: 60,000 SkyMiles + €117 per person. Four passengers = 240,000 SkyMiles + €468 (about $543). Fare class NL, 9 seats showing. Total elapsed CDG→MIA is 16h05.
blocks.flag: More than double the outbound award — 240,000 SkyMiles against 110,000 on Aer Lingus. The same Delta metal may be bookable through Virgin Atlantic or Air France/KLM Flying Blue for materially fewer points. Price both before spending 240K.

blocks.title: Atlanta — 3h47 layover
blocks.detail:
• US immigration and customs happen HERE, not Miami — first port of entry
• Recheck bags after customs, then back through security to the domestic concourse
• The long layover is doing real work: it absorbs the immigration queue without risking the Miami leg
• Proper sit-down meal here — it is the last one of the trip and everyone will need it

blocks.title: Late lunch at ATL
blocks.detail:
• After customs and re-clearing security, on the domestic concourse
• Plenty of choice on Concourse B/T — this is the one meal today that is not on a plane

blocks.title: Delta 1328 · Atlanta → Miami
blocks.detail:
• Home, arriving 7:15 PM
• Snack service only — everyone ate at Atlanta

ideas.title: ⚠ TRIP-BREAKER — Leavenworth collision
ideas.detail: This trip is Dec 16–28, 2026. Leavenworth Winter 2026 is Dec 19–27, 2026 with MIA→SEA booked on Dec 19 (Alaska AS305, conf UUKHNQ) and a Hampton Inn on 308K Hilton points. They overlap by eight days and both depart from Miami. These cannot both happen. Nothing here should be booked until one of them moves.

ideas.title: 💰 BUDGET — the plan costs $6,190, not $5,000
ideas.detail:
Straight answer: built the way you asked, this comes to $6,190 in cash (plus 485,000 points). Your $5,000 cap needs $1,190 removed, and there is no painless way to find it — the fixed spine is already $3,000 (Chamonix hotel $1,935, flight taxes $659, both TGV legs $404) before anyone eats anything.

WHERE IT GOES: Dining $1,948 · Hotel $1,935 · Flights $659 · Transport $636 · Excursions $562 · Trains $404.

WHAT IS ALREADY SQUEEZED: breakfast is free in Paris and in-room everywhere else (€12/day, not €58) — that alone saves about $330. Both train days run on bought-ahead picnics. Two supper nights in Paris are room picnics. Only three sit-down lunches in thirteen days.

THE CUT MENU — pick $1,190 worth:
• Drop Courmayeur entirely (bus + park + lunch) −$266. Costs you the only tubing on the trip.
• Skip the Mer de Glace family pass −$172. The ice cave is the single best thing in Chamonix; if the cave has not opened, cut this without hesitation.
• Make Christmas Eve the only splurge, hotel bistro on the 25th −$110.
• Skip Planpraz, use the free valley train to Argentière for snow instead −$90.
• Annecy lunch as a bakery picnic instead of Chez Mamie Lise −$50.
• Skip the Seine cruise −$58.
• Paris market lunches as bakery picnics −$40.
• Chamonix hotel: Hôtel La Verticale at €1,511 instead of Pointe Isabelle −$182 (2★, central, no sauna, no bistro).
• RER B instead of the CDG taxi on arrival −$16, and RER instead of the Gare de Lyon taxi on the 27th −$50. Both cost you an hour and stairs with luggage.

TAKING ALL OF THEM lands at roughly $5,156 — and removes tubing, the ice cave, the gondola and the boat. My honest read: that guts the trip to save $1,000.

WHAT I WOULD ACTUALLY DO: take the Christmas-dinner trim, the Annecy lunch, the Paris picnic lunches and the Gare de Lyon RER (−$250), accept about $5,900, and treat the $5,000 as the target you miss by a little rather than the reason to cancel the snow. The other real lever is lodging: a self-catering apartment with a kitchen would cut the Chamonix dinner line far harder than any of the above, but every Chamonix apartment I could price came in at or above Pointe Isabelle.

ideas.title: 🏨 Chamonix hotel alternatives — the shortlist
ideas.detail:
POINTE ISABELLE (current pick), €1,668/6 nights, 3★, quadruple room, sauna + gym + bistro, 3 min to both stations, 4 min to centre. 4.3/5 from 379. No pool, no kitchen.

HÔTEL L'OUSTALET, 330 rue du Lyret, €1,715 published tariff (5 nights Xmas band €280 + 26 Dec New Year band €315), 3★ family room, HEATED OUTDOOR POOL, 4.7/5 from 331 — best guest score of any 3★. But breakfast is extra (€17 adult / €12 child ≈ €360 a week), there is NO restaurant, and it is 12 min to the station.

HÔTEL DE L'ARVE by HappyCulture, 60 Impasse des Anémones, est. €1,400–1,900, 3★, GAMES ROOM + INDOOR CLIMBING WALL, sauna, family apartments. 4.4/5 from 831. Reviewers cite tired rooms — ask for a refurbished one.

APPART'HÔTEL LE GÉNÉPY, 16 Impasse du Génépy, est. €1,700–2,400, FULL KITCHEN, linens and cleaning included, 4.6/5 from 175 — best-reviewed self-catering in town. Only 13 units. Some units have winding stairs and windowless rooms — insist on a 3-room unit.

ODALYS ISATIS, 25 Chemin de Saint Roch, est. €1,400–2,000, 4★ residence, 1-bed apt ~34m², KITCHENETTE + DISHWASHER, part-covered heated pool, sauna, gym. Overlooks road or railway with a 7am first train, and ~11 min to the centre. Its own calendar showed no bookable December date — may be sold out.

MGM LE CRISTAL DE JADE, 174 Allée des Aiguilles, est. €2,600–3,800, 5★ residence, TRUE 2-BEDROOM 50m² apartment, INDOOR HEATED POOL, spa. The honest 'trade up' for this family — real beds for the kids rather than a sofa bed. Soundproofing between units is criticised.

LES AIGLONS, 270 Av de Courmayeur, est. €1,900–2,700, 4★, Junior Suite 40m² sleeps 4, heated outdoor pool, Italian restaurant on site. 4.1/5 from 1,788 — weakest 4★ score, and furthest out.

HÔTEL MONT-BLANC, 62 Allée du Majestic, est. €4,000–6,000, 5★, most central address in town, heated outdoor pool + Clarins spa, suites 75m². Breakfast €35pp = €840 for the week.

LE HAMEAU ALBERT 1er, 38 Route du Bouchet, est. €3,500–5,500, 5★, independent chalets, indoor-outdoor pool, and a second relaxed restaurant with a €17 children's menu so you are not trapped in fine dining.

ideas.title: Hotel pricing is validated, not inflated
ideas.detail: L'Oustalet publishes a rate card: family room €280/night in the 19–25 Dec band. Pointe Isabelle works out at €278/night. Two independent 3★ hotels within €2 of each other means ~€280 is simply the market rate for a Chamonix family room that week — the current pick is priced correctly. Note also that only the night of 26 December crosses into the higher New Year band, so checking out on the 27th dodges almost all of the New Year premium.

ideas.title: ⚠ BOOK 30 SEPTEMBER — the whole rail spine
ideas.detail: SNCF opens sales for 13 Dec 2026 – 6 Jan 2027 on Wednesday 30 September 2026, around 05:45. Both TGV Lyria legs depend on it. Buy a Carte Avantage Adulte (€49) BEFORE booking — −30% for the holder and one companion adult, −60% for both children aged 4–11, turning roughly €316 of one-way fares into about €174. The €89 capped fare does NOT apply on Lyria: SNCF guarantees those caps on domestic TGV INOUI and INTERCITÉS only.

ideas.title: ⚠ Sunday 27 December loses three of eight Geneva–Paris trains
ideas.detail: On Sundays the 06:28, 10:27 and 12:27 Geneva departures do not run, leaving a six-hour hole between 08:21 and 14:27 — on the last Sunday of the French school holidays when the whole valley turns over. The 14:27 is the plan and the tightest capacity point of the trip. Book it first.

ideas.title: 🍽️ How the food budget is actually held down
ideas.detail:
BREAKFAST: free in Paris (Regency Club), in-room from the Super U shop everywhere else — about €12 a day instead of €58. Across the trip that alone saves roughly €280.
LUNCH: Christmas-market chalets in Paris, packed picnics on both train days and at Planpraz, takeaway in Chamonix. Only three sit-down lunches all trip.
DINNER: bouillons in Paris (mains €7–13), Poco Loco and Elevation 1904 in Chamonix, two in-room picnic suppers, and exactly two splurges — Christmas Eve and Christmas Day.
The single biggest lever is the Paris hotel breakfast: at €25 per person it would be €100 a morning, €400 across the stay. Confirm Regency Club access covers both rooms.

ideas.title: 🚆 Train food — what is actually on board
ideas.detail:
TGV Lyria 2nd class is 'Standard'. There IS a bar car, 'Le Bistrot', on the UPPER deck. There is NO at-seat service in 2nd class — you walk to it, up an internal staircase, on a moving train.
Prices: club sandwich €7.50, croque monsieur €9.90, cheeseburger €9.90, pizza margherita €9.90, quinoa salad €12.50, hot dish €15.40–15.80. Menu Sandwich (sandwich + dessert + drink) €13.50. Hot chocolate €4.50, croissant €2.70, cookie €4.00, compote €3.90.
There is a 'Menu Enfants' section but no discounted children's set — a child eats for about the same as an adult.
VERDICT: board with food already bought. Four Menu Sandwich combos = €54; the same picnic from Monop'Daily is €40–50 and from the Monoprix opposite the station €25–35. Use the bar car as a mid-journey treat outing for hot chocolate instead, around 11:15 before the lunch rush.
Bringing your own food is fine — Swiss customs explicitly permit ready-to-eat food and non-alcoholic drinks for the day of travel.

ideas.title: 🛒 Chamonix food map
ideas.detail:
SUPERMARKETS: Super U, 117 rue Joseph Vallot — 6–8 min walk, Mon–Sat 08:15–19:30, Sun 08:30–12:00 ONLY. Carrefour Market, 339 Route Blanche — further out, Mon–Fri 08:00–19:30, Sun to 12:30, and confirmed 08:30–18:00 on 24 December.
BAKERIES: La Panière, 31 Place de l'Église and 118 rue Whymper — opens 06:00, the cheap pick. Le Fournil Chamoniard, 204 Av de l'Aiguille du Midi. Couloir, 204 Av Michel Croz — 40 m from the hotel.
CHEAP EATS: Poco Loco, 47 rue du Docteur Paccard, daily 10:00–22:00, burgers/crêpes/takeaway. Elevation 1904, opposite the station, 07:30–01:30 daily. MBC, 350 Route du Bouchet, burgers and a toy box, from 16:00. Le Bartavel, 26 cour du Bartavel, wood-fired pizza. ELA Deli, 11:00–21:30.
KIDS' MENUS with published prices: Le Vert Hôtel €8, Satsuki €10–13 (288 rue Joseph Vallot), Rocky Pop €12 (Les Houches), Héliopic €15.
AVOID on budget: anything fondue/raclette-led (L'M, Boccalatte) runs €80–120 for four.

ideas.title: ⚠ Christmas Day closures — shop on the 23rd
ideas.detail: Do the big shop on 23 December covering 24–26 December. Carrefour Market's confirmed 24 Dec hours (08:30–18:00) are the safety net. Assume NOTHING is open on the 25th — reports conflict, and any supermarket that opens will be mornings only. Bakeries generally do open. The Richard Bozon pool is confirmed closed all day on the 25th and closes 18:00 on the 24th; the ice rink has not published 24/25 December hours, so phone +33 4 50 53 12 36. Lifts and Les Planards do run — it is their peak revenue week. The tourist office publishes a 'restaurants with Christmas menus' page in November.

ideas.title: Carte d'Hôte — free valley trains
ideas.detail: Free at check-in at Pointe Isabelle. Unlimited free travel on the Mont-Blanc Express between Servoz and Vallorcine, covering Les Houches, Les Praz, Argentière and Vallorcine. Turn-up-and-go with no tickets is genuinely useful with young kids — you can bail home whenever someone melts down, and it makes Christmas Day afternoon free. Since the December 2023 relaunch it is NOT a bus ticket, only a discount on Chamonix Mobilité passes.

ideas.title: 🚇 Paris transport — pay as you go, nothing else
ideas.detail:
The 2025 fare reform abolished zones. One flat Métro–Train–RER ticket is €2.55 in 2026, valid anywhere in the region. Children 4–9 pay half: €1.30. Both children qualify for the whole trip.
Carnets no longer carry any discount as of 1 Jan 2026 — ten tickets cost ten times €2.55.
CHEAPEST OPTION: Navigo Easy cards (€2 each, non-refundable) loaded pay-as-you-go. Three days for the family works out at about €70 including the Montmartre funicular — against €147.60 for day passes and €191.40 for Paris Visite. Do not buy a pass.
One card cannot hold adult and child fares at the same time, so buy at least two — budget €8 for four and ask at the Porte Maillot window on arrival.
Note: the Métro–Train–RER ticket does NOT transfer to buses or trams (those are €2.05 separately), and the funicular ticket does not allow an onward transfer.

ideas.title: ✈️ CDG arrival — Terminal 1, and what food is there
ideas.detail:
Aer Lingus arrives at TERMINAL 1, confirmed across five flight-tracker and reference sources. Aer Lingus is IAG-owned but not oneworld, so it does not sit with BA/Iberia in the T2 halls — it has been at T1 for about twenty years. Check the boards on the day anyway.
There is effectively NO food between the aircraft door and the arrivals hall — arriving passengers do not pass the Level 4 airside outlets. Feed everyone on the flight or at Dublin.
LANDSIDE: Marks & Spencer Food on the arrivals level (Level 5, 06:30–20:30) is the only food outlet on that level — grab-and-go, cheapest sensible option, and directly on the way out. Down on the CDGVAL level: McDonald's public zone, 06:00–22:00, 450 m², table service AND a children's play area — the best hot meal for a family at T1. Also Brioche Dorée, Caffè Ritazza, Relay/Petit Casino (cheapest), and Le Grand Comptoir brasserie (€70–100+, too dear).
The T1 airside McDonald's is permanently closed, and Hippopotamus on the CDGVAL level closed in early 2026 — some online guides are stale.
Taxi rank is Level 5, Exit 24, past the car-rental desks, so a sit-down meal means going down and back up with bags.

ideas.title: ⚠ EES border queues at CDG
ideas.detail: The EU Entry/Exit System went fully live in France on 10 April 2026. First entry requires a passport scan, facial image and four fingerprints for the adults; children under 12 are exempt from fingerprinting. Reported Terminal 1 waits run 60–90 minutes at peak, and 13:00–18:00 is named as a peak band — a 12:45 arrival lands right at the edge of it. Budget 1h15–2h from wheels-down to the arrivals hall. Those wait figures come from commercial airport-guide sites, not from ADP or the border police, so treat the precision with caution. Keep snacks in hand luggage: the queue is where the kids will crack.

ideas.title: Courmayeur must be booked two days ahead this time
ideas.detail: The SAT Mont Blanc bus requires a reservation by 17:00 the previous day via savda.it or estore.arriva.it. The previous day is 23 December, when you are in Annecy all day — so book it on the 22nd. €30 adult / €15 child return, about 45 minutes through the Mont Blanc tunnel.

ideas.title: Fun Park Dolonne is the tubing fix
ideas.detail: Chamonix and the French side of the valley have no dedicated tubing run. Fun Park Dolonne at Courmayeur has a tubing run, a bobsled track, a beginner slope with magic-carpet lifts, and a soft-play area with inflatables and trampolines. Prices are not published — reportedly you can pay per activity rather than buying a day pass, which suits a half-day. Phone +39 366 268 6776 and confirm 24 December hours specifically.

ideas.title: Alpine Coaster — both kids ride with an adult
ideas.detail: Minimum age 3 seated with an adult; minimum height to ride alone is 1.35 m, which neither child will meet. So one family descent uses two sledges, and the 6-ride card at €47.50 buys three descents together. Runs 11:00–17:30 daily in winter, lit in the evening over Christmas. No lift pass needed for the coaster or the sledging area.

ideas.title: Ice cave opens only days before arrival
ideas.detail: The Mer de Glace ice cave is re-carved each autumn and does not open with the train. Montenvers indicates the ice-cave combination from 13 December; in 2025/26 it slipped to 20 December. Re-verify in late November. The train and the glacier viewpoint stand on their own if it has not opened — and if it has not, skip the €148 family pass and spend the day on the free valley train instead.

ideas.title: Annecy is forecast-dependent
ideas.detail: Annecy sits at 447 m in a basin prone to winter temperature inversions — you can leave a bright Chamonix morning and arrive in flat grey fog. December averages 7°C, ~57% cloud and a 30% chance of a wet day. The whole appeal is outdoors and there is no wet-weather fallback. Decide 48 hours out on the forecast; if it is fogged in or raining, swap it for a local Chamonix day.

ideas.title: Passports for everyone, including both children
ideas.detail: The Geneva legs cross into Switzerland and the Courmayeur day crosses into Italy. Switzerland is in Schengen but not the EU customs union, so the border is staffed and spot-checks happen; France has also reintroduced temporary internal Schengen checks. Bus operators on the Courmayeur run require ID regardless. Every traveller needs their own document — a child can no longer travel on a parent's passport.

ideas.title: Return flight is 4 × 60,000 SkyMiles
ideas.detail: The Delta award shows 60,000 points + €117 per person. For four that is 240,000 SkyMiles + €468 — more than double the outbound Aer Lingus award. Nine seats showing at NL fare. Price Virgin Atlantic Flying Club and Air France/KLM Flying Blue on the same Delta metal before spending 240K.

ideas.title: Hyatt House CDG — confirm one room or two
ideas.detail: Modeled at 15,000 points as given. The Paris stay uses two rooms; if the airport night also needs two, that is 30,000. Confirm before counting the balance. Also confirm the first shuttle run — you need to be at CDG by about 06:40 for a 9:10 departure.

ideas.title: Confirm the Paris award rate doesn't price peak
ideas.detail: 15,000 points per night is the Category 4 standard rate at the Hyatt Regency Étoile. Category 4 peak is 18,000, and the week before Christmas is a plausible peak window. Across two rooms and four nights that is the difference between 120,000 and 144,000 points. Separately, confirm that Regency Club breakfast covers the SECOND room — it normally attaches only to the member's room, and paying for breakfast would add roughly €400 to the Paris leg.

ideas.title: Aer Lingus award space is exactly four seats
ideas.detail: 4 seats at 27,500 points + $29.10 each — no margin. 110,000 points + $116.40 for the family. Confirm which currency this prices in (Avios is the likely route on Aer Lingus metal). The Dublin connection is 1h35m against the 1h45m–2h Aer Lingus itself recommends for US arrivals continuing into Europe.

ideas.title: 📞 Calls to make in November
ideas.detail:
Les Planards — Alpine Coaster Christmas-week hours, and whether sledges are hired or sold.
Patinoire Richard Bozon +33 4 50 53 12 36 — winter hours, 24/25 December opening, and whether they have support frames for young children.
Montenvers — the ice cave's actual opening date.
Fun Park Dolonne +39 366 268 6776 — prices, hours and 24 December opening.
Pointe Isabelle restaurant +33 4 50 53 12 87 and Le Cap Horn +33 4 50 21 80 80 — festive menus for the 24th and 25th, the week they publish.
Chamonix tourist office +33 4 50 53 00 24 — the Christmas programme, not published until late November.
Hyatt Regency Étoile — Regency Club access for the second room.
Hyatt House CDG — room count and first shuttle departure.
